title: Sultanate of Mempawah
capsule: The Sultanate of Mempawah was an Islamic Malay polity on the northern coast of West Kalimantan (Borneo), emerging from earlier Dayak-Hindu predecessor states. Its Islamic sultanate era was inaugurated by Opu Daeng Menambun (r. 1740–1761), a Bugis noble from the Luwu Kingdom of South Sulawesi, who introduced Islam as the official religion and established the ruling dynasty. From 1787 the Dutch East Indies authorities systematically influenced succession, making the sultanate increasingly dependent; British occupation of the region during the Napoleonic Wars further disrupted governance. The last sultan, Muhammad Thaufik Accamuddin, was taken prisoner by Japanese forces in 1944 and never returned, effectively ending dynastic rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's existence and rulers are documented through Dutch colonial records and local chronicles, but territorial extent—particularly in the interior—is poorly mapped and relies on approximate administrative boundaries rather than precise survey data.
